entities.summary:
Hugh of Remiremont (c.1020 – c.1099), called Candidus or Blancus (both meaning "the white"), was a medieval cardinal.

A member of the powerful Gelasian dynasty, Hugh was born into a family of high-ranking clergy and politicians.

In 1064, he was appointed as the Bishop of Remiremont, a position he held until his death in 1099.

Hugh played a significant role in the politics of the Holy Roman Empire, serving as a papal legate and participating in several key councils, including the Council of Clermont.

He was also a key figure in the Investiture Controversy, which pitted the Catholic Church against the Holy Roman Empire.
